items.question: Phase II drug metabolism reactions are mainly?
items.explanation: Phase II = conjugation (glucuronidation, sulfation, acetylation), making drugs more water-soluble for excretion.

items.question: Which antiarrhythmic is a class III agent?
items.explanation: Amiodarone is a class III (potassium channel blocker) but has all four Vaughan-Williams actions. Watch for thyroid, lung toxicity.

items.question: Which is an ultra-short-acting beta blocker used IV?
items.explanation: Esmolol has a half-life of about 9 minutes (hydrolysed by esterases), used for intra-operative tachycardia and hypertension.

items.question: Adrenaline is the drug of choice in?
items.explanation: Adrenaline (IM) is first-line in anaphylaxis: it reverses bronchospasm, vasodilation and hypotension.

items.question: Post-marketing surveillance corresponds to which phase?
items.explanation: Phase IV (pharmacovigilance) detects rare or long-term adverse effects after marketing in the general population.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 06 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Phase II drug metabolism reactions are mainly?
Ans: Conjugation
Why: Phase II = conjugation (glucuronidation, sulfation, acetylation), making drugs more water-soluble for excretion.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Cardiovascular)
Q: Which antiarrhythmic is a class III agent?
Ans: Amiodarone
Why: Amiodarone is a class III (potassium channel blocker) but has all four Vaughan-Williams actions. Watch for thyroid, lung toxicity.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Autonomic Nervous System)
Q: Which is an ultra-short-acting beta blocker used IV?
Ans: Esmolol
Why: Esmolol has a half-life of about 9 minutes (hydrolysed by esterases), used for intra-operative tachycardia and hypertension.

🌍 *FMGE* (Autonomic Nervous System)
Q: Adrenaline is the drug of choice in?
Ans: Anaphylaxis
Why: Adrenaline (IM) is first-line in anaphylaxis: it reverses bronchospasm, vasodilation and hypotension.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Clinical Trials)
Q: Post-marketing surveillance corresponds to which phase?
Ans: Phase IV
Why: Phase IV (pharmacovigilance) detects rare or long-term adverse effects after marketing in the general population.
